evaluations.3: Fiora was already posting strong numbers before the nerf. Average RP moved up, but win rate and placement rate fell.
evaluations.5: Zahir took a meaningful throwing-weapon mastery nerf, but his current meta numbers are still holding up well.
evaluations.6: Crossbow Nadine was already in a solid position, and the attack speed mastery buff pushed her numbers higher. Pick rate, win rate, and average RP are all strong, so she remains a good ranged carry option.
evaluations.8: The per-level attack power buff has not produced a meaningful statistical change. The rise of Katja, Adriana, and other characters that can punish Hart in poke standoffs is likely affecting the result.
evaluations.13: Shoichi received a Q slow-duration buff, but his early elimination risk remains a major issue. His aggregate numbers are still weak.
evaluations.15: Sissela's early durability buff improved her early fights, reducing the chance of being eliminated before stabilizing.
evaluations.17: Adriana's average RP rose sharply after the mobility cooldown buff. The change improved both her survival tools and her fight control.
evaluations.18: Shoichi received an E damage buff, but assassin metrics are broadly weak in the current environment, so the island still looks difficult for him.
evaluations.21: The intent to reduce Rozzi's control over melee opponents seems to have landed, but she is still a strong pick.
evaluations.29: The mobility buff appears to help Leon take fights and avoid early eliminations.
evaluations.33: Nicky received her first buff in a while. The passive and E buffs appear meaningful for a character that struggled throughout last season, with RP, win rate, and pick rate all trending upward.
evaluations.35: Tonfa Yuki received a second consecutive buff. With tonfa Yuki's average RP rising, players who moved to glove Yuki may want to reconsider tonfa.
evaluations.38: The passive cooldown reduction did not directly affect combat enough to move Jenny's numbers meaningfully.
evaluations.45: Mai's Exclusive buff does not appear to have a major impact in solo ranked play.
evaluations.47: Laura received a baseline stat buff through movement speed and skill amplification per level. Her numbers were already reasonable, and this should help her more against bruisers and ranged carries.
evaluations.51: Priya was buffed, but the change has not produced a meaningful statistical signal.
evaluations.52: Adina gained movement speed, but the change does not look like a meaningful buff by itself.
evaluations.55: Estelle was already posting good metrics, and the damage buff is reinforcing that trend. She looks worth choosing when the team needs a tank.
evaluations.56: Piolo has been nerfed twice in a row. His damage keeps being trimmed, but his utility is still preventing average RP from falling meaningfully.
evaluations.59: Isaac received another buff through attack power per level and passive damage. Even with a pick-rate increase that likely brought in less experienced players, his average RP improved, so he needs more observation through the next patch.
evaluations.61: Irem received a passive buff alongside a new skin. The skin effect appears to have raised pick rate and brought in many less experienced players, so her real trend needs more time.
evaluations.63: Ian was already in a decent position and received a useful buff. The W damage increase is pushing every major metric upward.
evaluations.66: Arda was performing well in high-tier games before the nerf. The ultimate cooldown increase is serious, but his numbers are still serviceable for now.
evaluations.69: Leni's defense and stun-duration nerfs are showing up in stability. Her average RP has fallen.
evaluations.70: Tsubame was weak before the patch, and this buff has not been enough to lift her numbers.
evaluations.71: Kenneth received a second consecutive buff. His previous buff did not fix the metrics much, but the added W damage-reduction buff has improved every major number.
evaluations.72: Katja received a per-level attack power buff and is showing good numbers. Despite a pick-rate increase that likely brought in less experienced players, average RP and win rate rose slightly.
evaluations.73: Charlotte improved in win rate, average RP, and placement rate after the Q damage buff. Her average RP is still deeply negative, so the buff response is visible but the pick remains inefficient for climbing in solo ranked.
evaluations.74: Darko is having a difficult season. The buff seems to respond to concerns about his value compared with Bihyung, but the late shield increase still looks insufficient.
evaluations.77: Yumin's Q damage was nerfed after she had been posting stable numbers. There is no major impact yet, so the rest of the patch should be watched.
evaluations.83: Henry only received a simple per-level health nerf. His average RP dipped slightly, but the overall impact is limited.
evaluations.84: Blair was nerfed for the first time in a while after a strong season start. Average RP rose, but win rate fell, suggesting the Q scaling nerf is having some effect.
evaluations.87: Coreline's empowered mirror projectile speed was nerfed. She had been stable across tiers, and this appears to have had some impact.
evaluations.88: Bihyung's strong baseline stats were nerfed again. His metric lead has narrowed, so the next trend needs more observation.

guide.title: ER&GG turns Eternal Return ranked data into practical meta context
guide.body: Character tiers, trio compositions, and weapon choices are not ranked by win rate alone. ER&GG compares win rate, pick rate, average RP, placement rate, and sample size together, with the current patch as the default context.
guide.metricsBody: Win rate measures first-place conversion, placement rate measures placement stability, and average RP reflects ranked climb efficiency.
guide.comboBody: A strong composition should have role coverage, stable average RP, and enough sample size instead of only one high metric.
guide.cautionBody: Low-pick or low-sample data can be biased toward specialists, so tier lists and team results should be read conservatively.

fallback.title: Current patch meta is summarized with ranked decision metrics, not win rate alone
fallback.body: ER&GG organizes Eternal Return ranked data across character tiers, trio compositions, weapon choices, and patch changes. Win rate is treated as first-place conversion, placement rate as placement stability, average RP as climb efficiency, and pick rate with sample size as context for reliability. The same character can read differently by patch, tier, team role, and weapon choice, so the current patch is used as the default baseline. Character pages and patch notes connect current statistics with balance changes.

memberActions.openControlledTarget: Create the team’s go signal with the first control while follow-up damage is in range.
memberActions.punishEnemyEntry: Stop the enemy after they spend their engage tool and cannot retreat safely.
memberActions.openDiveAngle: Create an angle that reaches the same target at the same time as the follow-up diver.
memberActions.confirmPokeAdvantage: Commit only onto a target whose health or mobility was reduced by poke.
memberActions.startFrontlineContact: Hold the nearest threat and create the first contact point for allied damage.
memberActions.followInitiatorTarget: Join the target held by the initiator and overlap the first damage window.
memberActions.syncDiveSameTarget: Reach the same target with the initiator and close off its escape route.
memberActions.screenCarry: Stay between the main damage dealer and incoming threats to preserve damage uptime.
memberActions.alternateFrontline: Step forward when the other frontline retreats and take over enemy attention and cooldowns.
memberActions.compressMeleeSpace: Compress the same area with the other melee members and block the target’s retreat.
memberActions.denyApproach: Use range and control to deny approach paths so allies are not forced to tank damage.
memberActions.holdFollowupRange: Hold the frontline without moving beyond allied follow-up range.
memberActions.repeatPoke: Repeat pressure from safe maximum range and track resources lost by the target hit.
memberActions.damageAfterPoke: Convert the health or mobility advantage created by poke into the main fight’s damage.
memberActions.applySafeFollowupDamage: Add follow-up damage to the engaged target while maintaining a safe range.
memberActions.damageControlledTarget: Commit primary damage to the target caught by the first control.
memberActions.damageNearestThreat: Keep attacking the nearest threat crossing into the team’s formation.
memberActions.damageExposedBackline: Focus the backliner outside protection range when allied engages overlap.
memberActions.damageIntrudingDiver: Attack the enemy that spent mobility to enter the formation and remove them inside it.
memberActions.chainControlOnTarget: Apply the next control as the first control ends on the same target.
memberActions.holdControlForDiver: Save control until the enemy diver spends mobility and can be stopped reliably.
memberActions.suppressApproach: Keep threatening the enemy’s approach path to restrict their mobility and engage timing.
memberActions.protectPrimaryDamage: Prioritize peel and protection so the primary damage member can keep attacking.
memberActions.finishCurrentTarget: Finish the target receiving allied damage, then decide the next action.

memberAvoids.doNotEnterAlone: Do not enter before the rest of the team can follow.
memberAvoids.doNotLeaveFollowupRange: Do not chase beyond allied follow-up range.
memberAvoids.doNotOverlapFrontCooldowns: Do not spend every defensive and control cooldown with the other frontline.
memberAvoids.doNotSplitMeleeTarget: Do not split onto a different target from the other melee members.
memberAvoids.doNotOverchase: Do not abandon the frontline to chase deep into the enemy backline.
memberAvoids.doNotCrossFrontline: Do not step ahead of the frontline and expose yourself to engage.
memberAvoids.keepEscapeTool: Do not spend all mobility offensively and become defenseless against the next engage.
memberAvoids.doNotSpendDefensiveToolEarly: Do not spend key protection or control before the enemy commits.
memberAvoids.doNotSpendSuppressionEarly: Do not spend every key denial tool on empty poke while the enemy can still engage.
memberAvoids.doNotChangeTargetEarly: Do not split damage onto a new target while the first target is still alive.

statements.pokeBeforeCommit: Create a health or mobility advantage with poke before spending frontline health to commit.
statements.syncBurstWindow: Layer the first control and all three key damage tools inside a target's defense and escape window.
statements.preserveCarryUptime: Give the main dealer time to keep hitting the same target from behind the frontline.
statements.rotateFrontline: Alternate which frontliner absorbs attention and major skills to extend backline damage uptime.
statements.compressMeleeSpace: Compress one area so all three members fight the same target within mutual melee range.
statements.preserveRangedSpacing: Avoid a static front fight and alternate range and mobility instead of letting one member tank too long.
statements.sustainAccessibleTarget: Keep damaging an accessible target instead of forcing an unreliable chase onto the backline.
statements.pokeThenCommit: Commit only after poke creates a health lead, forces mobility, or connects into follow-up control.
statements.waitEnemyEntry: Counter when the enemy has spent an engage tool and can no longer retreat safely.
statements.syncDiveEntry: Start the full fight only when at least two entry angles can reach the same target together.
statements.controlThenCommit: Use the first control hit or a key escape being spent as the signal for everyone to commit.
statements.frontlineContact: Connect damage after the frontline absorbs a key enemy tool or pins the nearest threat.
statements.controlledTarget: Prioritize the target all three members can actually reach after the first control, not a role name.
statements.nearestThreat: Remove the nearest enemy threatening your formation instead of forcing access to the backline.
statements.exposedBackline: Target a backliner outside protection and escape range only when multiple entries can land together.
statements.intrudingDiver: Stop and focus an enemy who has spent mobility to enter your formation.
statements.screenCarry: Stay between the main dealer and enemy divers instead of chasing the enemy backline too deeply.
statements.alternateAggro: Do not spend both frontliners' survival and control tools together; one holds the line as the other exits.
statements.collapseSameZone: Do not chase separate enemies; narrow escape and protection space together around one area.
statements.preserveRangedSpace: Deny approaches by alternating range, mobility, and control zones rather than assigning one member to tank.
statements.holdFollowupRange: Advance only as far as you can survive without leaving follow-up damage range.
statements.repeatPoke: Repeat the range advantage with poke while the other members prepare follow-up on the target it reaches.
statements.overlapBurst: Do not split targets while the first target lives; layer follow-up entry and burst onto that target.
statements.sustainNearest: Keep sustained damage on the nearest accessible enemy even as the active frontliner changes.
statements.sameTargetDistributed: Even without one carry, overlap all three major damage tools on the same target and timing.
statements.resetOnMiss: If the opening control or burst misses, disengage instead of feeding the remaining key tools one by one.
statements.regroupOnSeparation: If frontline, backline, or melee members separate, regroup before continuing the chase.
statements.reopenDistance: If the catch fails or mobility is spent, reopen distance and create the next damage turn.
statements.switchWhenOutOfRange: When the current target leaves effective range, immediately switch to the next threat entering it.
statements.chaseOnlyEscapeSpent: Chase briefly only after a kill or a key escape has been confirmed as spent.
statements.fightBeforePoke: Avoid a solo frontline commit before poke creates an advantage and splits the team's damage.
statements.staggeredEntry: Avoid entering one at a time and being isolated before the next member arrives.
statements.frontlineOverextends: Avoid chasing the enemy backline so deeply that the carry and protection owner are separated.
statements.simultaneousFrontCooldowns: Avoid spending both frontliners' survival and control cooldowns together with nothing for the next enemy turn.
statements.splitMeleeTargets: Avoid turning triple melee into three separate duels and losing the numbers advantage.
statements.spendAllMobility: Avoid both ranged members using mobility aggressively at once and becoming exposed to the next engage.
statements.splitDamage: Avoid all three members attacking different targets and finishing none of them.

combatInstructions.holdFormation: Keep frontline-to-backline spacing so follow-up damage can still reach after the first engage.
combatInstructions.maintainRange: Do not collapse all three at once; pressure from maximum poke range and draw out health or mobility first.
combatInstructions.holdCompact: Overlap protection ranges while leaving enough space to avoid all three being hit by one control effect.
combatInstructions.splitAngles: Create separate entry angles, but synchronize them so the first spotted member never fights alone.
combatInstructions.staggerFrontline: Decide who absorbs pressure first so both frontliners do not spend survival and control tools together.
combatInstructions.assignSignal: Choose one control or tactical skill as the go signal and hold the remaining major cooldowns.
combatInstructions.controlOrEscape: Commit only when the first control lands or a key enemy escape has been spent.
combatInstructions.pokeAdvantage: Create a health lead or force mobility with poke, then use the first control hit as the focus signal.
combatInstructions.enemyCommit: Counter when the enemy has actually spent an engage tool and can no longer retreat cleanly.
combatInstructions.isolatedTarget: Enter only when a target leaves protection range and both approach angles can connect together.
combatInstructions.frontlineContact: Start after the frontline absorbs a key enemy tool or pins the nearest threat in place.
combatInstructions.agreedControl: The other two members commit to the same target only after the agreed first control lands.
combatInstructions.openOneTurn: Complete the opening duty without overchasing, preserving range and an angle for the next member.
combatInstructions.sameTarget: Do not split targets while the first one lives; layer follow-up entry and main damage in order.
combatInstructions.nearestThreat: The backline should remove the nearest threat crossing the frontline instead of forcing access to the enemy backline.
combatInstructions.protectThenDamage: Stop the diver's movement first to create damage uptime, then turn onto that exposed target together.
combatInstructions.alternateCooldowns: Step forward as the previous member's key tool ends, alternating survival and control cooldowns.
combatInstructions.finishOrReset: Chase briefly after a kill or key escape is spent; if the first entry fails, reset formation and cooldowns first.
combatInstructions.repeatPokeOrReset: If the catch fails, do not force the chase; reopen distance and create another poke turn.
combatInstructions.holdOrReset: Keep clearing the nearest target while the formation holds; regroup immediately if frontline and backline separate.

combatPlans.engageChain: The initiator draws attention, the follow-up diver locks onto the same target, and the third member concentrates damage.
combatPlans.pokeCatch: Chip opponents from range, then focus one target when the first control skill connects.
combatPlans.frontToBack: The frontline holds space while the backline removes the nearest threat and the third member denies dives.
combatPlans.counterEngage: Stop the enemy engage with protection or displacement, then counter-focus the exposed target.
combatPlans.collapse: Collapse on a priority target from different angles, remove them quickly, and create a numbers advantage.
combatPlans.brawlCycle: Stagger frontline and sustained-fight cooldowns to keep a long close-range fight going.
combatPlans.coordinate: Use the first control hit as the signal and commit all three major tools to the same target in sequence.

patternDescriptions.threeLayer: The tank creates space while the support extends the main damage dealer's uptime.
patternDescriptions.diveFollow: The initiator draws attention first, then a mobile teammate follows onto the same target.
patternDescriptions.doubleFront: Two members hold the front while a backline dealer applies sustained damage.
patternDescriptions.frontToBack: The frontline starts or absorbs the engage so the backline can finish from a safe range.
patternDescriptions.protectCarry: The support preserves the main dealer's position and survival for a longer fight.
patternDescriptions.pickBurst: The comp focuses on deleting an isolated target to create a numbers advantage.
patternDescriptions.pokeKite: The comp chips first, maintains range, and punishes forced approaches.
patternDescriptions.brawl: The comp repeatedly engages and trades at short range to win a direct fight.
patternDescriptions.flexible: No single plan dominates, so the team must agree on who engages and who protects before fighting.

powerSpikes.formationReady: when frontline and protection tools are ready with the carry's key skills
powerSpikes.burstCooldowns: when engage, burst, and control can land on the same target
powerSpikes.frontlineReady: when frontline survival and backline sustained damage are ready together
powerSpikes.rangeSetup: after securing vision and range with poke and escape tools available
powerSpikes.sustainedResources: while healing, defense, and sustained-fight resources remain
powerSpikes.synchronizedTools: when all three members' ultimates, tactical skills, and weapon skills overlap

favorable.singleDive: isolated one-by-one dives that can be counter-engaged
favorable.exposedBackline: backlines with limited protection or escape tools
favorable.shortRangeApproach: short-range opponents forced to approach through the frontline
favorable.slowFrontline: slow frontlines with limited forced-engage options
favorable.closeRangeFight: fights where both teams must stay close and keep trading
favorable.conditional: fights where the engage owner and focus target are agreed in advance

threats.splitPressure: multi-angle pressure that separates frontline, support, and carry
threats.peelDisengage: strong peel, knockback, or disengage stopping the first entry
threats.flankCollapse: flanks reaching the backline or a large gap opening behind the frontline
threats.hardEngage: hard engage that closes distance before poke can create an advantage
threats.longRangeKite: losing health to long-range poke and disengage before making contact
threats.unclearInitiation: unclear engage ownership causing key skills to be used separately
